kaikki_vikisozluk.e: وَبَش or وَبْش • (wabaš or wabš) m (plural أَوْبَاش (ʔawbāš))
kaikki_vikisozluk.t:
From the root و ب ش (w b š). The primary meaning of the root relates to dispersion and heterogeneous mixture: the noun originally denoted scattered or mixed elements of any kind — people, plants, or spots on skin. The collective أَوْبَاش (ʔawbāš) may alternatively derive, according to some medieval lexicographers (Ibn Manẓūr, Lisān al-ʿArab), as a metathesized form of بَوْش (bawš, “crowd, throng”).
The medical sense (white spots on fingernails) is attested in the earliest Arabic lexicography as the primary concrete referent of the root, while the social senses (rabble, riffraff) developed as figurative extensions of the image of scattered, mixed fragments.
g: rabble, riffraff; a mixed, disreputable crowd; people of low origin or no fixed social standing
vagabond, rowdy; a person without fixed abode or respectable standing (singulative use)
a scattering of mixed or heterogeneous vegetation; sparse, mixed scrub
leuconychia; leukonychia; white spots or flecks appearing on the fingernails
nonsense; the dross or refuse of speech; faulty, worthless talk
rl: أَوْشَاب — cited as synonym by al-Aṣmaʿī
